hypothesis.causal_defect: The detector can seed both rejection and acceptance for one liquidity event, while the preserved ordinary FAR transition checks only rejection_seed. This permits an acceptance-origin or unresolved mixed auction to be silently relabelled by generic reclaim, MSS and displacement.
hypothesis.single_strategy_change: Ordinary FAR is eligible only when rejection_seed is true and acceptance_seed is false. A mixed or acceptance-origin event remains non-FAR until a future independent candidate defines and observes an explicit acceptance-failure transition.
hypothesis.unchanged: Liquidity detection, pool identity, draw resolution, market-leadership semantics, FAR confirmation geometry, entry, stop, target, costs, current-NAV 3% sizing, session I7 module, global arbitration and NautilusTrader execution/accounting are unchanged.
hypothesis.interpretation_rule: The interval was previously inspected as Candidate 14 L1. It is reused only to test whether the categorical transition explains the observed failure mechanism; no result from this branch can establish success.

research_question: When one 84-day NautilusTrader account is replayed unchanged except for exclusive FAR auction-origin ownership, are the mixed-origin losses removed without creating new logic, execution or opportunity failures?

selection.method: Controlled replay of the previously inspected Candidate 14 L1 interval. Dates, data, costs, risk, execution and all other strategy rules are unchanged so the one categorical transition can be isolated. This interval is permanently ineligible for a success claim or future holdout use.

strategy_change_control.single_change: ordinary FAR requires exclusive rejection origin
